items.title: Jefferies initiates coverage on Leela Hotels with Buy rating, sees 22% upside
items.description: Jefferies initiated coverage on Leela Hotels with a Buy rating and a Rs 675 target, citing India’s premiumisation trend, rising luxury travel demand and the company’s owned-led expansion strategy. The brokerage expects strong revenue and earnings growth through FY29, supported by higher room rates, leisure exposure and Brookfield backing.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc, Vedanta, Nalco and other metal stocks slide up to 5%. Here's why
items.description: Metal stocks tumbled up to 5% on Monday, with the Nifty Metal index falling over 2% amid a decline in metal prices and rising expectations of higher-for-longer US interest rates. Profit booking after the index’s strong August rally also weighed on sentiment, while Jefferies remained bullish on Hindustan Zinc over Hindalco.

items.title: Tejas Networks among 6 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 28, six Nifty500 stocks that gained over 5% were identified using the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is rising, suggesting strengthening price momentum in the stock. This may signal potential upward movement and can be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: Ashoka Buildcon shares rally 10% after securing Rs 602 crore order from RVNL
items.description: Ashoka Buildcon shares surged over 10% after the company received a Rs 602.16 crore order from Rail Vikas Nigam Limited for electro-mechanical works across four railway tunnels in Uttarakhand. The 30-month project is expected to strengthen the company’s order book, while the stock’s technical setup also remains in focus.

items.title: 20 stocks, 100% returns: How retail investors tapped a multibagger wave in deeper Indian market
items.description: Retail investors enjoyed impressive returns by picking specific stocks wisely. Over the last year, numerous companies showcased returns exceeding one hundred percent. Sectors like telecom and capital goods led the way, with high-beta and event-driven stocks also providing significant rewards. Ultimately, careful stock selection played a more vital role than merely concentrating on sector performance for achieving these gains.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares after Jagdishan: What lies ahead for the country’s largest private lender?
items.description: HDFC Bank's CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan plans to retire in October 2026 following a major merger, leaving investors eager for details on his successor and the bank's future direction. The institution encounters hurdles in attracting deposits and enhancing margins post-merger. Experts propose either a temporary internal leader or an external hire. In the meantime, stock performance may remain subdued until the next leadership is established.

items.title: ₹49 lakh crore market-cap wipeout! Are Nifty’s fallen giants bargains or value traps?
items.description: India's leading stocks have witnessed a staggering loss of forty-nine lakh crore rupees in total market capitalization. A significant decline has affected forty-seven companies within the Nifty index, with heavyweights like TCS, HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, and Infosys leading the charge. Analysts are divided over whether these diminished stocks present enticing investment opportunities or merely serve as potential pitfalls.

items.title: Sensex falls 300 points, Nifty below 24,100 amid multiple headwinds. What lies ahead?
items.description: On Monday, Indian stock indices Sensex and Nifty dipped significantly, with broader market indices like Nifty Smallcap and Midcap also experiencing more severe declines. Major players like Infosys and Tata Steel were among those causing the downturn. In a contrasting trend, HDFC Bank shares managed to rise, reflecting an unusual market sentiment dominated by sellers, leading to more declining stocks than advances.

items.title: Lenskart shares to rally 40%? Nomura initiates coverage with Buy, says its growth journey has just started
items.description: Lenskart has emerged from challenger to market leader, with Nomura initiating coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and Rs 888 target, implying around 40% upside. The brokerage sees a long growth runway driven by store expansion, strong market positioning, vertical integration and a cost advantage, while MSCI inclusion could also attract passive inflows.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares gain over 2% as CEO Jagdishan rejects new term; Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, others weigh in
items.description: HDFC Bank's Managing Director, Sashidhar Jagdishan, has opted against reappointment, prompting brokerages to uphold their positive stance on the bank's stock. In light of this announcement, the board has hastened efforts to find a suitable successor. Analysts appreciate this proactive approach as it alleviates concerns and promises potential value. Investors’ attention now shifts to the upcoming leadership transition and its expected impact on future growth prospects.

items.title: Ather Energy among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On August 28, four Nifty500 stocks that gained over 6% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period, and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Is Nifty set for a breakout? Analysts see signs of a shift ahead
items.description: Nifty hovered near 24,175, needing to clear 24,200 to regain strength. Analysts suggest bullish option spreads for rebounds and caution against a 23,900 break. HEG and Laurus Labs are recommended buys with specific targets and stop losses. Glenmark Pharmaceuticals and Shipping Corporation of India also present buying opportunities. Newgen Software and Elgi Equipments show positive chart setups for investors.

items.title: Augmont Enterprises shares debut at 22% premium over IPO price
items.description: The Rs 825 crore IPO, priced at Rs 788 per share, comprised a fresh issue of 79 lakh shares worth Rs 620 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 26 lakh shares aggregating Rs 205 crore. Ahead of the public issue, the company had also raised Rs 246.30 crore from anchor investors.

items.title: MSCI rebalancing threatens to turn ‘Messy’ in new Indian auction
items.description: This Monday marks a critical juncture for India's new closing auction system, as it gears up to manage an influx of billions in passive fund trades. The quarterly MSCI index rebalancing is expected to catalyze heightened trading volume, putting the system’s reliability under scrutiny. Both market participants and regulators are keenly awaiting how smoothly it addresses large institutional orders in this high-stakes environment.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 6 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, six stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 28, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend in a particular stock.
